messages.subject: Re: dplyr: Oracle and MS SQL?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Hadley,

I've had a go at running the rsqlserver package, but it may not be robust enough yet to be used by dplyr.

That said, I've been following your instructions above to try to get Oracle working using the ROracle package.

I've managed to get src_oracle and tbl() working correctly, but have had to hack ROracle to do it.

Here are some issues I've found:
Oracle throws an error for statements ending  ";" when using ROracle
The "AS" in "SELECT id, name FROM (SELECT id, name FROM x) AS y" throws an error. The correct syntax is to omit the "AS" part when it relates to sub-queries. Here below are a few valid examples of alias names for tables and columns.
SELECT id AS my_id, name AS my_name FROM (SELECT id, name FROM x) y
SELECT id my_id, name my_name FROM (SELECT id, name FROM x) y
SELECT id my_id, name my_name FROM (SELECT id, name FROM x)
LIMIT doesn't work in Oracle. The equivalent is something like this:
> SELECT outer.*
>   FROM (SELECT ROWNUM rn, inner.*
>           FROM (  SELECT e.*
>                     FROM employee e
>                 ORDER BY hiredate) inner) outer
>  WHERE outer.rn >= 5 AND outer.rn <= 10

So src_oracle() and tbl() now "work" but I've had to modify ROracle to strip out the semi-colons, AS, and LIMIT it finds in SQL statements.

What's the best way to change dplyr to get those working for real? It seems those issues are hard-coded and there isn't currently any code make the functions act differently for different tbl_xxx objects.

Most of what I do with plyr seems pretty straightforward in dplyr, but one thing that I can't find in the docs is the equivalent of mdply. Does it mean I'm stuck loading the two packages (potential clashes), or have I missed an equivalent statement? If it's also faster, great, but I think most of the time the applied function is the bottleneck anyway.

Minimal example,

require(plyr)
p = expand.grid(mean=1:5, sd=seq(0, 1, length=10))
mdply(p, rnorm, n=5)

Regards,

baptiste

messages.subject: Re: unexpected expressions in dplyr select
messages.body_plain:
All of the dplyr verb use non-standard evaluation, so it's possible to
break them all with a little work. I'm happy with the current trade
off in select() - converting column names to numeric indices is nice
because then : and - have a trivial implementation.

OTOH, changing the implementation to use custom : and - functions
inside of select would have the advantage of making richer selection
operations (e.g. https://github.com/hadley/dplyr/issues/158) easier to
implement. I'll keep thinking about it.

Hadley

messages.subject: dlply and do
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I have used dlply() function from "plyr" in the past to obtain linear regression with  the following code:

reg <- function(df) {
  lm( y ~ x,  data=df)
}

reg.check <- dlply(df, .(variable), reg))

I get an output list based on the "variable"

When I try to run the equivalent using do() function from dplyr:

new2 <- group_by(df, variable)
reg.check <- do(new2, reg)

I get the same as dlply(), but lose the "variable" assignment.

Is there anyway to get exactly the same output of dlply() using do()?

Thanks,

Gerardo

messages.subject: Re: dlply and do
messages.body_plain:
Hi Gerardo,

I've just started working on the next iteration of dplyr. I think it's
going to work like this:

new2 <- group_by(df, variable)
reg.check <- do(new2, reg = lm(y ~ x, data = .))

Then you'll get a data frame with a column variable (the group labels)
and reg (a list of models). Then you can use that with other dplyr
functions.

# extract all r squared values
summarise(reg.check, r2 = summary(reg)$r.squared)

# extract coefficients
do(reg.check, coef(.))

Hadley

I think that's only used in one place in dplyr
(qry_fields.DBIConnection) so it should be an easy fix.

> The "AS" in "SELECT id, name FROM (SELECT id, name FROM x) AS y" throws an
> error. The correct syntax is to omit the "AS" part when it relates to
> sub-queries. Here below are a few valid examples of alias names for tables
> and columns.
>
> SELECT id AS my_id, name AS my_name FROM (SELECT id, name FROM x) y
> SELECT id my_id, name my_name FROM (SELECT id, name FROM x) y
> SELECT id my_id, name my_name FROM (SELECT id, name FROM x)

Ok, so that means dplyr needs a method for naming subqueries - I think
I'm already using the from function consistently, so it needs to be
made into a generic and added to dbi-s3.r with an appropriate name.

> LIMIT doesn't work in Oracle. The equivalent is something like this:
>
> SELECT outer.*
>   FROM (SELECT ROWNUM rn, inner.*
>           FROM (  SELECT e.*
>                     FROM employee e
>                 ORDER BY hiredate) inner) outer
>  WHERE outer.rn >= 5 AND outer.rn <= 10

LIMIT is only used in a handful of places, and may not even be
necessary. I using limit for (e.g.) head(tbl) but it's redundant with
the number of rows supplied to fetch. My initial thinking was this the
LIMIT would help the database optimise the query (because it would
know that it doesn't need to compute more than n rows), but I don't
think most (any?) databases actually do that optimisation.

> What's the best way to change dplyr to get those working for real? It seems
> those issues are hard-coded and there isn't currently any code make the
> functions act differently for different tbl_xxx objects.

go? I'm happy to review pull requests as you go.

Anyway, I'm fairly certain I've ironed out the issues with Oracle and done so without (hopefully) breaking anything else.

The main difference is the addition of sql_as() generics to name sub-queries in a manner that works in Oracle (i.e. without an "AS").

I've also changed head.tbl_sql() to use build_query(x)$fetch(n) instead of build_query(x, limit = n)$fetch() thus avoiding the use of LIMIT entirely, as per your comments. Note that I haven't removed any of the code that could work with LIMIT in SQL; just removed the need for it by changing head.table_sql().

I made a minor change to utils.r unique_name(); table name is now "W_" , instead of "_W", which did not work in Oracle.

As you described in a previous note, the rest of the changes were pretty straightforward; just generics for OraConnection.

I don't yet have qry_explain.OraConnection() working, nor lahman_oracle(), but it looks like all of the single and binary verbs are working correctly.

messages.subject: dplyr filter behavior
messages.body_plain:
hey

I can't figure out if this is a bug or just an improper use of dplyr. I'm trying to use a vector from a data frame to subset a tbl and it seems to elicit an error.

So I have this tbl:

d1 <- tbl_df(data.frame(num1 = as.character(sample(1:10, 1000, T)),
                        var1 = runif(1000)))
d1$num1 <- as.character(d1$num1)

which I want to subset according to values I find in this data frame

d2 <- data.frame(num1 = 1:3)
d2$num1 <- as.character(d2$num1)

If I pass the num1 values as a separate character vector, everything works great

d1 %.%
  filter(num1 %in% c("1", "2", "3")) %.%
  group_by(num1) %.%
  summarise(mu = mean(var1))

> Source: local data frame [3 x 2]
>
>   num1        mu
> 1    2 0.4662081
> 2    1 0.4810027
> 3    3 0.4920704

But if I pass the restriction as variable in a data frame:

d1 %.%
   filter(num1 %in% d2$num1) %.%
   group_by(num1) %.%
   summarise(mu = mean(var1))

> Source: local data frame [0 x 2]

This is despite the ostensible similarity between both restrictions

identical(c("1", "2", "3"), d2$num1)
> [1] TRUE

Am I missing some obvious? It would seem like this would be useful, to subset a tbl via values in a data frame.

messages.body_plain:
dplyr has revolutionized things for me, so thanks a lot for that and your SF Meetup presentation.  I have since switched a lot of production code to it for the obvious performance benefits, and read/usability benefits over other packages.

I seem to crash R a lot with it, and here is an example (using R3.0.2, dplyr 0.1.2):

I have 2 tbls, A and B, both grouped by the same 2 variables.
I do an 'outer_join' on them (which is actually an rbind of (left_join(A,B), anti_join(B,A)) after adding missing columns and reordering columns).

This outer_join leaves me a fresh tbl called error_rates, which has no grouped variables.

There are no NAs in this dataset, as I know they have caused problems.

Now I want to mutate variables, so I didn't think I need to group_by.  However, if i don't group_by, I get a Segmentation fault: 11

 *** caught segfault ***
address 0x8, cause 'memory not mapped'

Traceback:
 1: .Call("dplyr_mutate_impl", PACKAGE = "dplyr", df, args, env)
 2: mutate_impl(.data, named_dots(...), environment())

Explicitly, this is what causes segfault:

error_rates <- error_rates %.%
    mutate(
      ntwkRev = sum( rev, na.rm = TRUE),
      lev_pRev   = round( rev / ntwkRev, 5),
      ntwkImp = sum( imp, na.rm = TRUE),
      lev_pImp   = round( imp / ntwkImp, 5),
      ntwkError = sum( error, na.rm = TRUE),
      lev_pError   = round( error / ntwkError, 5),
      activity = error + imp,
      errRate = error / ( imp + error),
      ntwk_errRate = ntwkError / ( ntwkImp + ntwkError),
      #deviation = 1/(1 + exp(-pError)) - .75,
      importance = round( 1000 * (errRate - ntwk_errRate)^3 * errRate * lev_pError, 3)
    )

This produces results as expected:

error_rates <- error_rates %.% group_by( var1_level, var2_level) %.%
    mutate(
      ntwkRev = sum( rev, na.rm = TRUE),
      lev_pRev   = round( rev / ntwkRev, 5),
      ntwkImp = sum( imp, na.rm = TRUE),
      lev_pImp   = round( imp / ntwkImp, 5),
      ntwkError = sum( error, na.rm = TRUE),
      lev_pError   = round( error / ntwkError, 5),
      activity = error + imp,
      errRate = error / ( imp + error),
      ntwk_errRate = ntwkError / ( ntwkImp + ntwkError),
      #deviation = 1/(1 + exp(-pError)) - .75,
      importance = round( 1000 * (errRate - ntwk_errRate)^3 * errRate * lev_pError, 3)
    )

Note that when I then %.% arrange(desc(importance)) I get another segfault because importance has NaNs.  Perhaps these NaNs produced by the mutate division by 0 are causing the segfault.

Perhaps this is all expected.  Please let me know if it is.  If not, let me know if I can dig deeper to help debug.

Thanks.
